# Sandfort documentation

> Sandfort is a self-hosted sandbox server for running AI-generated code. It offers a REST API, a Python SDK and a CLI over isolated Docker sandboxes. The server is source-available under FSL-1.1-Apache-2.0, and the SDKs and the CLI are Apache-2.0.

## Pages

- [API reference](https://docs.sandfort.dev/): Sandfort REST API reference, rendered from the OpenAPI specification.
- [Sandfort hosted beta: quickstart](https://docs.sandfort.dev/quickstart): One page from delivery package to a working sandbox. Every step here is a condensed copy of the connect guide, when anything is unclear or fails, the guide section named in each step is the...

- [Operations runbook](https://docs.sandfort.dev/operations): This runbook covers two deployments: Kubernetes (the kit in deploy/k8s/) and docker compose (deploy/compose.prod.yml, which the hosted beta VM uses). Sections and commands that apply to Kubernetes...
- [Security](https://docs.sandfort.dev/security): This page answers the questions a security team asks before a pilot. Each statement is checked against the server source, docs/architecture.md, [operations] or deploy/. Where a protection does not...
- [Isolation tiers](https://docs.sandfort.dev/isolation-tiers): Sandfort runs untrusted, often AI-generated code. Plain containers share the host kernel, so a kernel exploit inside one sandbox reaches the host. To let you pick a boundary per workload, Sandfort...
- [Releases](https://docs.sandfort.dev/release): A release is a git tag v0.1.0-beta.N on main, created after the gate passes. The tag fixes the commit. The artifacts are the Python SDK wheel, the CLI wheel and the server wheel (the sandfort...
- [Governance reference](https://docs.sandfort.dev/governance): For platform and compliance reviewers. Every statement here was checked against the server package (src/sandfort/), the source file is named where a reviewer may want to confirm it. Defaults are the...
- [Sandfort hosted beta: connect guide](https://docs.sandfort.dev/guide): > First time here? The quickstart is one page: > verify the delivery, install, first sandbox. This guide is the full reference behind it.

## Reference

- [OpenAPI specification (JSON)](https://docs.sandfort.dev/openapi.json): the exported spec for the REST API.
- [Sandfort landing page](https://sandfort.dev/): what Sandfort does, the ways to run it, isolation tiers and limits.
- [Landing page llms.txt](https://sandfort.dev/llms.txt): the llms.txt of the landing site.
- [Source code](https://github.com/malinele/sandfort): the server, Python SDK, CLI and MCP server in one repository.
